references.text: The burnt offering (עֹלָה) is mentioned here with the laying on of hands for atonement, as in Leviticus 14:20
The grain offering (מִנְחָה) is described here as part of the sacrificial system, corresponding to what is mentioned alongside the burnt offering
The priest makes atonement (כִפֶּר) for the sin, and the person is forgiven and made clean
The priest offers a burnt offering and makes atonement so that the woman becomes clean after childbirth
Part of the same cleansing ritual where the priest makes atonement for the one to be cleansed
A parallel text for the poor who cannot afford a full sacrifice, yet the priest still makes atonement and the person is made clean
The priest offers a burnt offering and a sin offering and makes atonement for the impurity
The priest offers the burnt offering and makes atonement for himself and the people
Atonement (כִפֶּר) at the altar to consecrate it, corresponding to the act of atonement in Leviticus 14:20
The book of Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
Christ offered himself once for all as the final sacrifice for cleansing and sanctification
